scenes.title: 2012 Sussex Behavioral & fMRI Suite: Silent Forearm-Scratching Screen Triggering Instant Mirror Itch vs Tapping Control
scenes.era: 2012, Sackler Centre for Consciousness Science, University of Sussex, Brighton, UK

layout.description: Sunlit cognitive neuroscience testing room with a crisp tabletop monitor displaying a cropped silent close-up of fingers scratching a forearm (paired beside a matched finger-tapping control frame), a 0-to-7 itch-rating button pad on the oak desk, and an adult observer trying not to scratch their own untouched sleeve.

positions.who: Adult study volunteer (42-year-old 2.5D matte cream-white vinyl figure in rolled-sleeve navy cotton sweater)
positions.where: seated facing the silent desktop display as their right hand involuntarily rises halfway from the button pad to scratch their untouched left forearm

positions.who: Sussex neuroscientist Henning Holle (2.5D matte cream-white vinyl researcher in smart tweed blazer and collared shirt)
positions.where: standing beside the control console toggling between the Scratching clip and matched Tapping control clip while logging the 64% scratch rate

props.name: desktop stimulus monitor showing cropped forearm scratching vs finger tapping
props.period_detail: faceless cropped upper-arm video frames isolating pure scratching motion from facial emotion (Holle et al. 2012)
props.physical_behavior: State-A calm finger-tapping control clip (viewer hands flat) -> State-B active forearm-scratching clip (viewer hand snaps up to own arm)

props.name: 0-to-7 itchiness rating button box and personality trait clipboard
props.period_detail: tracks the F=56.45 itch jump alongside neuroticism-over-empathy trait scores
props.physical_behavior: State-A resting at zero during tapping -> State-B pressed firmly at high itch score right after the 5-second scratch clip

actions.verb_sequence: switches silent monitor from finger-tapping control to forearm-scratching clip -> observes volunteer's immediate involuntary hand reach
watches silent scratching screen for 5 seconds -> reaches right hand briskly across to scratch untouched left forearm -> presses high rating button with a sheepish grin

reactions.reaction: startled wide-eyed blink and wry laugh catching their own hand mid-scratch on completely unbitten skin
notes strong neuroticism vigilance correlation and zero empathy link on the study chart

scenes.wardrobe: 2012 British academic attire: researcher in charcoal blazer and light-blue Oxford shirt; adult volunteer in rolled-sleeve navy knit crewneck and chinos.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key coastal Sussex daylight across pale oak desk and crisp monitor frame.
scenes.recognition_hook: Zero bugs, zero skin contact, zero sound — just five seconds of watching a stranger scratch on a silent screen makes 64% of healthy adults scratch their own arm!

key_visual.description: a sunlit Sussex neuroscience desk where an adult volunteer watching a silent close-up screen of a forearm being scratched reaches across to scratch their own untouched arm beside a 0-to-7 button pad

scenes.title: Sunlit Outdoor Park Patio Table: One Person Scratching Sets Off a Chain Reaction Across Friends
scenes.era: Modern sunlit outdoor neighborhood cafe patio & park bench

layout.description: Bright open-air wooden park picnic table under green afternoon trees where three middle-aged friends chat over iced coffee; one friend casually scratches an elbow and both companions across the table unconsciously rub their own neck and forearm within seconds.

positions.who: First patio friend (in linen button-down shirt)
positions.where: seated on the sunlit outdoor bench absentmindedly scratching their left elbow

positions.who: Two companion adults across the table
positions.where: glancing at the scratch motion and immediately rubbing their own unbitten forearm and collar in mirror sync

props.name: iced water glasses on sunlit outdoor wooden patio table
props.period_detail: everyday open-air social setting where visual scratch contagion spreads across a group — plus cool glass press to break the loop
props.physical_behavior: State-A resting on wooden table -> State-B cool glass pressed flat against forearm skin to calm the phantom prickle without raking nails

actions.verb_sequence: spot friend scratching elbow -> reach toward own forearm -> swap fingernail scratch for pressing the cool iced water glass calmly against skin

reactions.reaction: laughing in recognition at how fast the phantom itch jumped across the outdoor table

scenes.wardrobe: Relaxed adult weekend outdoor wear: rolled linen shirt, cotton polo, sunglasses resting on table.
scenes.lighting: Warm natural afternoon sunlight dappled across open park greenery and cafe terrace.
scenes.recognition_hook: One person scratches an elbow at an outdoor patio table, and five seconds later half the table is itching — until a cool flat press breaks the habit loop.

scenes.title: Wake Forest Saline-Drop Clinical Test: Visual Scratch Video Amplifying Body-Wide Itch 3.8x
scenes.era: 2011, Wake Forest Dermatology Clinic suite (Papoiu & Yosipovitch)

layout.description: Clean sunlit dermatology exam room with a tiny clear saline dropper bottle on a tray beside a video display showing scratching clips, illustrating how visual cues alone trigger body-wide itch.

positions.where: placing a single harmless saline drop on an adult patient's forearm before starting the visual clip
feeling phantom itch spread to completely untouched shoulder and opposite arm as soon as the scratching clip plays

props.name: clear saline control dropper and body-map distribution chart
props.period_detail: documents Papoiu et al.'s (2011) 3.8x widespread scratching jump on rash-free skin
props.physical_behavior: State-A neutral baseline under harmless saltwater -> State-B scattered body-map markers lighting up during visual scratch video

actions.verb_sequence: applies neutral saline control drop -> starts visual scratch clip -> logs widespread non-local itch sites on body chart

reactions.reaction: surprised realization that untouched opposite shoulder itches from pure visual input

scenes.wardrobe: Clean white dermatology coat; casual short-sleeve cotton polo and slacks.
scenes.recognition_hook: Put harmless saltwater on the left arm and play a scratching video — and volunteers start itching on their completely untouched right shoulder!

spatial_contrast_spec.landmark_or_object_a: Stranger scratching across an open table triggering instant visual-to-skin relay
spatial_contrast_spec.landmark_or_object_b: Cool palm pressure breaking the contagious scratch loop

spatial_contrast_spec.cut_b_topdown_3d_arrow: 90-degree top-down two-seat atrium table with a straight #FF2525 3D contagion arrow leaping directly from viewer to forearm
